about: a builder's hammer's short grey-brown hickory haft, a slight swell at its butt and a slim neck under the head, drawn in the hickory haft's skin (art/parts/axe/handles.png)

length_m.source: the reference hammer's, 0.33 m overall: a carpenter's 16 to 20 oz hammer is 13 in overall, a framing hammer 16 in (assets/data/kinds/hammer.json; recalled)

grip_from_end_m.source: the fist's middle a little under a hand's width up from the butt, the little finger 2 to 3 cm above the swell (assets/data/kinds/hammer.json; D546's hafted 0.04 to 0.12)

grip_diameter_m.source: the hatchet's 32 mm (short_hickory_haft.json): thinner handles sit badly in the fist; inside a power grip's range (holds.ts, NIOSH 2004-164)

profile_m.source: a hammer handle's shape: a low swell at the butt, a straight 32 mm grip a fist and a half long, then drawn down to a neck 21 to 25 mm across under the head, which whips a little, and a short shoulder into the eye's size (by eye, from wooden claw and cross-peen hammer handles; recalled)

density_kg_m3.source: hickory 600 to 930 kg/m^3, the middle (The Engineering ToolBox, Wood Species - Densities, engineeringtoolbox.com/wood-density-d_40.html, looked up 2026-10-28)
